issues: The week was quiet outside the weekend and covers per head were lower.
High Deliveroo prep times are attributed to drivers arriving early and checking in on the tablet before they reach the restaurant, not to kitchen delays.
Labour was high because an extra person was added at lunch on advice and proved unnecessary; labour must now be actively managed down through the quiet periods.
The weekly sales projection carried in the tracker was too high and has been revised down.
General manager and head chef meetings are to move to Sundays so the preceding week can be reviewed properly.
Reviews for the week were overwhelmingly five star, with one two star complaining of salty ramen and dry salmon.

A B2B partnership event runs tomorrow afternoon with a family and lifestyle group introduced through Go Southampton, with a discount button set up on the till; some tables are booked and the rest will arrive as walk ins.
Maintenance: the kitchen sink has been fixed and an electrician is booked to repair a kitchen socket.
The site's own areas for improvement are review volume and cleanliness.
A new front of house starter began on Saturday.
Preparation is under way for the boat show, with a staff limit of three people and takeaway packaging being ordered in line with the other sites.
Region-wide (South England): A standing daily performance target of ten app signups and ten Google reviews per site has been set, with a proposal to gamify it so the teams engage with it.

Region-wide (South England): Front of house sometimes ask for a review from a table that has had a poor experience; staff must read the table and check satisfaction before asking, and management should routinely check in on section status.
Region-wide (South England): Sites must report the status of their envelope returns to the office.
